Do not adopt Academy for the outer loop. That question is settled: LangGraph owns the main loop and state.

docs.title: Ten minutes with a mock campaign
docs.text:
In [1]: Copied! 
import importlib.util
import os
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys

CLONE = pathlib.Path("IMPRESS")
CHECKOUT = pathlib.Path("../..")  # when this notebook is run from inside the repository

# The campaign specs and the toolkits live in the repository, not in any wheel, so the
# clone is needed whether or not the package is already importable.
if not (CHECKOUT / "agent/campaigns").is_dir() and not CLONE.exists():
    subprocess.run(
        ["git", "clone", "--depth", "1",
         "https://github.com/radical-collaboration/IMPRESS.git", str(CLONE)],
        check=True,
    )

if importlib.util.find_spec("impress_a") is None:
    subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "-e",
         f"{CLONE}/agent[figures]"],
        check=True,
    )
    print("installed")
else:

def one_campaign(name, params, lab, salt=None):
    """One campaign, isolated the way the lab isolates a cell."""
    overrides = {**mock_lab.LAB_BASE, **mock_lab.ARM_BASE}
    if params:
        overrides["params"] = params
    cell = mock_lab.Cell(
        cell=name, kind="arm", arm=name, knob="", value=0.0,
        salt=salt or name, rep=0, model="D", overrides=overrides,
    )
    record = mock_lab.run_cell(cell, yaml.safe_load(BASE_SPEC.read_text()), lab)
    # `collect` joins against the manifest that the full sweep writes. One cell run by
    # hand has no sweep behind it, so write the one record it needs.
    (lab / "manifest.json").write_text(
        json.dumps({"cells": [record], "disclaimer": mock_lab.DISCLAIMER}, default=str)
    )
    # `collect` logs a row count per table. Useful for a full lab, noise here.
    lab_log = logging.getLogger(mock_lab.__name__)
    lab_log.setLevel(logging.WARNING)
    try:
        tables = mock_lab.collect(lab)
    finally:
        lab_log.setLevel(logging.NOTSET)
    return [r for r in mock_lab.read_table(tables["campaigns"])
            if r["arm"] == name][0]

docs.title: Ten minutes with a mock campaign¶
docs.text:
Location: agent/campaigns/

IMPRESS-A runs a campaign: it decides what experiment to run next, composes a workflow for it, puts that workflow through five gates, reads the results, and decides again. This notebook runs that loop on a laptop surrogate of the six-stage small-molecule binding chain -- the same executor, the same composer, the same gates, the same acceptance thresholds, and six tools that return in milliseconds.

You will run four campaigns, find two places where the system does something other than what it looks like it should, and then break a campaign on purpose and buy it back with knobs.

About two minutes end to end, plus a minute or two for the install.

!!! warning "Every metric here is a seeded random draw"

The mock tools model no chemistry. A number you see below is not a
measurement and says nothing about any molecule.

What **is** honest is the campaign's *behaviour* -- how many cycles it took,
which gate refused what, whether the Pareto front filled, where the control
plane spent its time -- because that is the same engine the real campaigns
run. A behaviour observed here is the behaviour the real campaign would
show. A number observed here is not a measurement.

docs.title: Setup¶
docs.text:
One editable install, of agent/ with the figures extra, which brings matplotlib. impress-a runs on the same middleware as the root impress package (radical.asyncflow over rhapsody) but does not depend on it, so nothing else needs installing first. Python 3.11 or newer: that is the floor radical.asyncflow and rhapsody set.

The install must be editable and from a clone: the tool registry resolves toolkits/ relative to the package's own file, so a wheel install finds no tools at all. (IMPRESS_A_TOOLKITS is the override if you ever need one.)

docs.title: What a campaign costs, before running one¶
docs.text:
impress-a offer answers two questions a caller has to ask before committing an allocation: what would this cost, and which goals could it actually address? It reads the toolkit, composes nothing and executes nothing.

That guarantee is in the signature rather than in the documentation: offer_for_spec is def, not async def, and no backend can be constructed without an awaited engine. A synchronous function cannot run a task however wrong its body gets.

Read the WARNINGS block at the bottom. Those are recorded defects with backlog identifiers, printed on every offer -- not a disclaimer.

docs.title: The four arms¶
docs.text:
Four settings of one campaign. They are named for what the campaign does, not for what the surrogate reports -- every mock metric is a random draw, so a name like "low-plddt" would be naming noise, while "aborted after three all-failed runs" is a control-plane outcome that reproduces.

Arm Setting What it should do baseline shipped defaults clears every bar; the Spec is satisfied; the front fills rescued difficulty: 0.55 plus three knobs raised the same difficulty, bought back hard difficulty: 0.55 an acceptance shortfall hopeless difficulty: 0.85 an integrity failure

hard and rescued are a matched pair at identical difficulty, differing only in the three knobs raised to buy it back. That is what separates "can knobs recover this campaign?" from "is this campaign hard?".

difficulty is the surrogate's own dial and has no counterpart on any real tool. It exists so you can make a campaign easy or impossible without editing a threshold. It is also marked operator_only: a campaign may set it, and no reasoner may propose it -- otherwise a model asked to satisfy the objectives would simply turn the difficulty down and nothing would say so.

Each arm runs as a subprocess with its own run root, its own trust ledger and its own seed salt. The ledger is the one that matters: trust is cross-run state, so a shared one would make the result a function of the order the cells ran in.

docs.title: Look at this before reading on¶
docs.text: The figure below is each arm's stop reason against what it actually had on the Pareto front. Find the disagreement yourself before scrolling.

docs.title: Trap 1 -- the stop reason is not the result¶
docs.text:
Three of the four arms stop on "every spec objective satisfied". Only two of them have anything on the front. hard reports success with an empty front and twelve failed lineages.

This is not an artefact of the surrogate. It is a real defect in the engine, tracked as backlog G14, and it comes from two halves of "is this campaign finished?" reading different evidence:

  • DataRegistry.ingest records a task's metrics whatever its QC verdict, and SatisfactionRule counts those readings.
  • core/pareto correctly refuses a FAILed node a place on the front.

So every objective has enough readings to look satisfied, while nothing has actually passed. It is unfixed on purpose: changing what satisfaction counts changes when the pre-registered campaigns stop.

The general lesson is the one worth carrying off this notebook. An autonomous system reporting that it is done is not evidence that it produced anything. The two have to be checked separately, which is why f6 plots them against each other.

docs.title: Two kinds of failing¶
docs.text: Now the per-stage funnel. The failures are split into acceptance shortfalls and integrity failures, and only one of those costs anything.

docs.title: Trap 2 -- acceptance and integrity are not degrees of the same thing¶
docs.text:
hard and hopeless both fail every lineage. They are not the same failure.

  • hard (difficulty 0.55) misses a quality bar. Every failure is an acceptance failure: the node FAILs, and the pattern's trust is untouched.
  • hopeless (difficulty 0.85) drives ss_fraction under the has_secondary_structure floor. That is an integrity failure: the node FAILs and the pattern is demoted.

The line sits at roughly 0.75, and it is a threshold rather than a slope. This is decision 0013, and it exists because counting quality thresholds against trust made promotion a function of how hard the target was -- one real job ran 30 tasks clean and promoted nothing.

Reaching for a dial to "make the campaign fail" without noticing which kind of failure you bought is the mistake this toolkit exists to make visible.

docs.title: Now predict, then run¶
docs.text: Set a difficulty and commit to a prediction before you run the next cell. Saying it out loud is the exercise; the gap between what the campaign looks like it should do and what it does is the thing being tested, not the numbers, which are drawn.

docs.title: Buy it back¶
docs.text:
Keep the difficulty where it is and raise three knobs: diffusion_steps to 200, packmin.cycles to 5, and diffusion_samples to 25. This is the rescued arm, and it is the matched partner of hard.

Which of the three did the work? f2 has the spans.

docs.title: What you just ran, and what it did not include¶
docs.text:
Everything above used model D -- the deterministic control: rules end to end, no language model, no network, no key. That is the reproducible baseline, and it is what the sweeps always use.

The lab has a second axis this notebook does not turn. --reasoners A and B replace the rules above the tools with a live model, and they need a profile in agent/models.yaml naming an endpoint plus a key in its environment variable. Two things are worth knowing before you reach for it:

  • The lab refuses a live model with no profile rather than quietly running the rehearsal. --model B without one runs RehearsalOracle and reports zero LLM calls -- which is exactly what a degraded live arm reports. A figure labelled "model B" drawn from the rehearsal is a manufactured void outcome, so the lab exits 2 and names what it refused, before spending anything.
  • It probes the endpoint once before any live cell, because a failure inside a campaign cycle is retried twice, recorded as reasoner_degraded, and then falls back to model D's cascade -- and the campaign exits 0. Without the probe you would get a full set of figures for a model that never answered.

There are no recorded LLM transcripts in this repository, so nothing here can replay a live run offline. If you do run one, check degraded_events in campaigns.csv before reading any of its yield.

docs.title: Three things to try¶
docs.text:
Run the sweeps. mock_lab.sweep(LAB, repeats=1, only=["sweeps"]) walks five knobs across their declared ranges, one cycle per cell, and f1 and f2 turn into response surfaces. About a minute.

Run an arm twice into the same trust directory. Verdicts move, because the pattern is already promoted the second time. This is why every cell above got its own ledger.

Set tool_delivery: real in the spec. The campaign is refused at validation rather than quietly reporting drawn numbers as science. That is gate 6, and it is the interesting mistake to make on purpose.

docs.title: Where to go next¶
docs.text:

  • Architecture -- the outer loop, the layers and the invariants.
  • Control Models -- what each of A, B, C and D is shown and what it may choose.
  • Decision 0013 -- trap 2, argued at length.
  • Known Limitations -- including the ones this notebook walked you into.
  • Small Molecule Binding -- the real chain these six surrogates stand in for.

def decide(
    current: dict,
    previous: dict,
    generation: int,
    cfg: ToyConfig,
) -> SpawnDecision:
    """The adaptive rule itself, as a pure function.

    Kept separate from the callback that runs on the engine so it can be tested
    without a `WorkflowEngine`, and so the notebook can show the rule without
    showing the plumbing around it.
    """
    degraded = tuple(
        v.target for v in verdicts(current, previous, cfg.degradation_threshold)
        if v.degraded
    )
    if generation >= cfg.max_generations:
        return SpawnDecision(
            False,
            f"no spawn: generation cap reached ({generation}/{cfg.max_generations})",
            degraded,
        )
    if len(degraded) < cfg.min_degraded_to_spawn:
        return SpawnDecision(
            False,
            f"no spawn: {len(degraded)} degraded, "
            f"{cfg.min_degraded_to_spawn} needed",
            degraded,
        )
    return SpawnDecision(
        True,
        f"spawn: {len(degraded)} degraded "
        f"({', '.join(degraded)}) exceeded threshold "
        f"{cfg.degradation_threshold}",
        degraded,
    )

docs.title: Watch IMPRESS adapt¶
docs.text:
Location: examples/colab/

Every other example in this repository needs an allocation, a GPU and model weights. This one needs a browser tab. It runs a real IMPRESS pipeline that watches its own results get worse and spawns a child pipeline to deal with it, and then shows you what that did to the run.

About 40 seconds end to end, plus a minute for the install the first time.

docs.title: What is real here, and what is not¶
docs.text:
Real: ImpressManager, WorkflowEngine on asyncflow's LocalExecutionBackend, executable tasks that start actual subprocesses, and genuine adaptive child-pipeline spawning through submit_child_pipeline_request.

Not real: the science. Every score below is a seeded pseudo-random draw and says nothing about any protein. What you are measuring is the framework's behaviour -- when it reacts, and what reacting costs -- not a property of a molecule.

docs.title: Setup¶
docs.text:
Installs impress and clones the repository for the helper module. Safe to re-run: it does nothing if the framework is already importable.

--no-deps is deliberate. impress declares radical.pilot, but never imports it -- the only radical import in its source is radical.asyncflow -- and radical.pilot ships as an sdist with a C extension. Skipping it turns a multi-minute cell into a few seconds. Install it normally when you are going to a real HPC backend.

docs.title: The rule the pipeline adapts on¶
docs.text:
A pipeline runs several passes over a set of targets. After each pass it calls await self.run_adaptive_step(wait=True), and the manager runs the adaptive function below against the live pipeline.

The rule compares this pass's score for each target against the last one. A target whose score fell by more than degradation_threshold is degraded. If enough targets are degraded, the pipeline hands them to a child pipeline and stops working on them itself -- the same shape as the real protein-binding example, which migrates degraded targets into a sub-pipeline.

Two details that are easy to get wrong, and that this notebook depends on:

  • The adaptive function must be a declared engine task, not a plain function. PipelineSetup raises TypeError otherwise, and so does a child configuration that carries a bare coroutine.
  • The generation cap is yours to enforce. The framework has no generation concept and no limit of its own. ImpressManager.start() returns when no pipeline is left, so a rule that always spawns never returns.

docs.title: Set the knobs¶
docs.text: degradation_threshold is the one to play with: it decides how big a drop counts as a target going wrong, so it directly controls how much the run adapts. Lower it and the pipeline spawns more children.

docs.title: Run it¶
docs.text:
Note the await with no asyncio.run around it. WorkflowEngine needs a running event loop and a notebook already has one, so asyncio.run fails here.

Watch for three things in the log:

  1. The six structure_prediction tasks of a pass all start at the same timestamp. Each is a real subprocess, and the pipeline collects their futures before awaiting any of them.
  2. The first adaptive_eval declines to spawn -- the first pass has nothing to compare against.
  3. When a spawn does happen, the parent's next pass runs over fewer targets. It handed them over.

docs.title: Where the time went¶
docs.text: Each bar runs from a task's submission to its future resolving. The gaps between passes are not task work: they are the manager's adaptive poll. It notices the flag on one 0.5s cycle and releases the pipeline on a later one, so every run_adaptive_step(wait=True) costs about a second. On a real run, where a task is a structure prediction, this is invisible. Here it is most of the clock, and it is worth seeing once.

docs.title: What the pipeline decided¶
docs.text: One arrow per submit_child_pipeline_request. The label names the targets the parent migrated and stopped working on.

docs.title: Why it decided that¶
docs.text:
The dark red lines are the targets the simulation makes fragile. Where one crosses into a child pipeline it turns blue and its slope flattens -- in this model a child buys time, it does not repair the target. The dotted line marks the spawn.

This is the figure to come back to after changing degradation_threshold: the trajectories do not move, only the point at which the framework decides they have gone far enough.

docs.title: How much ran at once¶
docs.text:
The peaks are one pass's targets running together.

The max_workers line is drawn for reference, and the run goes straight through it. That is correct, not a bug: executable tasks are subprocesses started on the event loop, so the thread pool does not bound them. It bounds function tasks and the adaptive callback.

docs.title: Turning the knob¶
docs.text:
The same run at five thresholds. Each one is a complete, independent run with its own engine -- which is also a check that the framework can be driven repeatedly in a single kernel.

Expect spawning to fall to zero as the threshold rises past the biggest drop any target takes, and the makespan to fall with it: adapting costs time.

docs.title: Three things to try¶
docs.text:
Set max_generations to 0. Spawning stops entirely and every adaptive_eval says why. This is the knob that keeps a recursive rule terminating; without a cap of your own, start() never returns.

Set degradation_threshold to 0.5. Almost any wobble counts as degradation, so the run spawns until it hits the generation cap. Compare the genealogy to the one above.

Set n_targets to 12. The concurrency figure's peaks double while max_workers stays where it is -- the demonstration that the thread pool is not what bounds these tasks.

docs.title: Where to go next¶
docs.text:
• Adaptive Execution -- the same mechanism, explained rather than run.
  • Architecture -- what the manager, the pipeline and the engine each own.
  • Protein Binding -- the real version of the rule used here: ProteinMPNN and Boltz-2 on Delta, migrating degraded targets into sub-pipelines.
  • Small Molecule Binding and Discontinuous Scaffolds -- two more production campaigns.
  • IMPRESS-A -- what happens when the decision above is made by an agent instead of a rule.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
This section documents the public classes that make up the IMPRESS core library: impress.impress_manager, impress.pipelines.impress_pipeline, impress.pipelines.setup, and impress.utils.logger. Each page below is generated directly from the source docstrings.

Module Class Description impress.impress_manager ImpressManager Orchestrates pipeline submission, adaptive-step execution, child-pipeline spawning, and lifecycle cleanup. impress.pipelines.impress_pipeline ImpressBasePipeline Abstract base class for user-defined pipelines; provides the adaptive execution and child-pipeline request protocol. impress.pipelines.setup PipelineSetup Pydantic model describing a single pipeline submission (name, type, config, adaptive function). impress.utils.logger ImpressLogger Colorized, level-filterable console logger used internally by the manager and pipelines.

See Architecture for a narrative overview of how these pieces fit together.

This section covers impress only. IMPRESS-A (impress_a) is a separate package, and its reference documentation is hand-written rather than generated from docstrings — it lives in its own section, not here.

docs.title: impress.utils.logger.ImpressLogger
docs.text:
Hand-rolled, optionally colorized console logger used internally by ImpressManager and ImpressBasePipeline.

Provides generic level-based logging methods (debug, info, warning, error, critical) as well as semantic convenience methods for specific pipeline/manager lifecycle events (e.g. pipeline_started, pipeline_failed, adaptive_completed). All levels are written to output_stream (default sys.stdout); messages below min_level are dropped.

Source code in src/impress/utils/logger.py 
class ImpressLogger:
    """
    Hand-rolled, optionally colorized console logger used internally by
    `ImpressManager` and `ImpressBasePipeline`.

    Provides generic level-based logging methods (`debug`, `info`,
    `warning`, `error`, `critical`) as well as semantic convenience methods
    for specific pipeline/manager lifecycle events (e.g.
    `pipeline_started`, `pipeline_failed`, `adaptive_completed`). All
    levels are written to `output_stream` (default `sys.stdout`); messages
    below `min_level` are dropped.
    """

    _LEVEL_ORDER = [
        LogLevel.DEBUG,
        LogLevel.INFO,
        LogLevel.WARNING,
        LogLevel.ERROR,
        LogLevel.CRITICAL,
    ]

    def __init__(
        self,
        name="ImpressManager",
        use_colors=True,
        output_stream=None,
        min_level: LogLevel = LogLevel.DEBUG,
    ):
        """
        Initialize the logger.

        Args:
            name: Logical name attached to `pipeline_log()` messages
                (typically the owning pipeline or manager name).
            use_colors: Whether to wrap output in ANSI color codes.
            output_stream: Stream to write all log messages to. Defaults
                to `sys.stdout`.
            min_level: Minimum severity to emit; messages below this
                level are silently dropped. Defaults to `LogLevel.DEBUG`
                (emit everything).
        """
        self.name = name
        self.use_colors = use_colors
        self.output_stream = output_stream or sys.stdout
        self.min_level = min_level

        self.level_colors = {
            LogLevel.DEBUG: Colors.BRIGHT_BLACK,
            LogLevel.INFO: Colors.BRIGHT_CYAN,
            LogLevel.WARNING: Colors.BRIGHT_YELLOW,
            LogLevel.ERROR: Colors.BRIGHT_RED,
            LogLevel.CRITICAL: Colors.RED + Colors.BOLD,
        }

        self.component_colors = {
            "pipeline": Colors.BRIGHT_GREEN,
            "adaptive": Colors.BRIGHT_MAGENTA,
            "manager": Colors.BRIGHT_BLUE,
            "workflow": Colors.CYAN,
            "task": Colors.YELLOW,
            "error": Colors.RED,
            "success": Colors.GREEN,
            "stage": Colors.BRIGHT_CYAN,
            "step": Colors.CYAN,
            "resource": Colors.MAGENTA,
            "data": Colors.BRIGHT_YELLOW,
            "validation": Colors.BRIGHT_MAGENTA,
            "checkpoint": Colors.BRIGHT_GREEN,
            "metric": Colors.BRIGHT_WHITE,
        }

    def _colorize(self, text, color):
        return f"{color}{text}{Colors.RESET}" if self.use_colors else text

    def _format_message(self, level, component, message, pipeline_name=None):
        timestamp = self._colorize(
            datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3], Colors.DIM
        )
        level_color = self.level_colors.get(level, Colors.WHITE)
        colored_level = self._colorize(f"[{level.value}]", level_color)

        # Handle pipeline-specific components
        if component.lower().startswith("pipeline-"):
            component_color = Colors.BRIGHT_GREEN
        else:
            component_color = self.component_colors.get(component.lower(), Colors.WHITE)

        colored_component = self._colorize(f"[{component.upper()}]", component_color)

        pipeline_part = ""
        if pipeline_name:
            pipeline_colored = self._colorize(f"[{pipeline_name}]", Colors.BRIGHT_WHITE)
            pipeline_part = f" {pipeline_colored}"

        return (
            f"{timestamp} {colored_level} {colored_component}{pipeline_part} {message}"
        )

    def _is_enabled(self, level: LogLevel) -> bool:
        return self._LEVEL_ORDER.index(level) >= self._LEVEL_ORDER.index(self.min_level)

    def _write_log(self, message):
        self.output_stream.write(message + "\n")
        self.output_stream.flush()

    def debug(self, message, component="manager", pipeline_name=None):
        """Log a DEBUG-level message.

        Args:
            message: Message text to log.
            component: Named component tag used for color-coding (e.g.
                "manager", "pipeline", "adaptive").
            pipeline_name: Optional pipeline name to include in the log line.
        """
        if not self._is_enabled(LogLevel.DEBUG):
            return
        formatted = self._format_message(
            LogLevel.DEBUG, component, message, pipeline_name
        )
        self._write_log(formatted)

    def info(self, message, component="manager", pipeline_name=None):
        """Log an INFO-level message.

        Args:
            message: Message text to log.
            component: Named component tag used for color-coding.
            pipeline_name: Optional pipeline name to include in the log line.
        """
        if not self._is_enabled(LogLevel.INFO):
            return
        formatted = self._format_message(
            LogLevel.INFO, component, message, pipeline_name
        )
        self._write_log(formatted)

    def warning(self, message, component="manager", pipeline_name=None):
        """Log a WARNING-level message.

        Args:
            message: Message text to log.
            component: Named component tag used for color-coding.
            pipeline_name: Optional pipeline name to include in the log line.
        """
        if not self._is_enabled(LogLevel.WARNING):
            return
        formatted = self._format_message(
            LogLevel.WARNING, component, message, pipeline_name
        )
        self._write_log(formatted)

    def error(self, message, component="manager", pipeline_name=None):
        """Log an ERROR-level message.

        Args:
            message: Message text to log.
            component: Named component tag used for color-coding.
            pipeline_name: Optional pipeline name to include in the log line.
        """
        if not self._is_enabled(LogLevel.ERROR):
            return
        formatted = self._format_message(
            LogLevel.ERROR, component, message, pipeline_name
        )
        self._write_log(formatted)

    def critical(self, message, component="manager", pipeline_name=None):
        """Log a CRITICAL-level message.

        Args:
            message: Message text to log.
            component: Named component tag used for color-coding.
            pipeline_name: Optional pipeline name to include in the log line.
        """
        if not self._is_enabled(LogLevel.CRITICAL):
            return
        formatted = self._format_message(
            LogLevel.CRITICAL, component, message, pipeline_name
        )
        self._write_log(formatted)

    def pipeline_started(self, pipeline_name):
        """Log that a pipeline has started.

        Args:
            pipeline_name: Name of the pipeline that started.
        """
        colored_name = self._colorize(pipeline_name, Colors.BRIGHT_WHITE)
        message = f"Pipeline started: {colored_name}"
        self.info(message, "manager")

    def pipeline_completed(self, pipeline_name):
        """Log that a pipeline has completed.

        Args:
            pipeline_name: Name of the pipeline that completed.
        """
        colored_name = self._colorize(pipeline_name, Colors.BRIGHT_WHITE)
        message = f"Pipeline completed: {colored_name}"
        self.info(message, "manager")

    def pipeline_failed(self, pipeline_name, exc):
        """Log that a pipeline's task finished by raising an exception.

        Args:
            pipeline_name: Name of the pipeline that failed.
            exc: The exception raised by the pipeline's `run()` task.
        """
        colored_name = self._colorize(pipeline_name, Colors.BRIGHT_WHITE)
        message = f"Pipeline FAILED: {colored_name} — {exc}"
        self.error(message, "manager")

    def pipeline_killed(self, pipeline_name):
        """Log that a pipeline was killed via `kill_parent`.

        Args:
            pipeline_name: Name of the pipeline that was killed.
        """
        colored_name = self._colorize(pipeline_name, Colors.BRIGHT_WHITE)
        message = f"Pipeline killed: {colored_name}"
        self.warning(message, "pipeline")

    def adaptive_started(self, pipeline_name):
        """Log that a pipeline's adaptive function has started.

        Args:
            pipeline_name: Name of the pipeline whose adaptive function
                started.
        """
        colored_name = self._colorize(pipeline_name, Colors.BRIGHT_WHITE)
        message = f"Adaptive function started for: {colored_name}"
        self.info(message, "adaptive")

    def adaptive_completed(self, pipeline_name):
        """Log that a pipeline's adaptive function has completed.

        Args:
            pipeline_name: Name of the pipeline whose adaptive function
                completed.
        """
        colored_name = self._colorize(pipeline_name, Colors.BRIGHT_WHITE)
        message = f"Adaptive function completed for: {colored_name}"
        self.info(message, "adaptive")

    def adaptive_failed(self, pipeline_name, error):
        """Log that a pipeline's adaptive function raised an exception.

        Args:
            pipeline_name: Name of the pipeline whose adaptive function
                failed.
            error: String description of the error.
        """
        colored_name = self._colorize(pipeline_name, Colors.BRIGHT_WHITE)
        message = f"Adaptive function failed for {colored_name}: {error}"
        self.error(message, "adaptive")

    def child_pipeline_submitted(self, child_name, parent_name):
        """Log that a child pipeline has been submitted by its parent.

        Args:
            child_name: Name of the newly submitted child pipeline.
            parent_name: Name of the parent pipeline that submitted it.
        """
        colored_child = self._colorize(child_name, Colors.BRIGHT_WHITE)
        colored_parent = self._colorize(parent_name, Colors.BRIGHT_WHITE)
        message = f"Submitting child pipeline: {colored_child} from {colored_parent}"
        self.info(message, "manager")

    def manager_starting(self, pipeline_count):
        """Log that the manager is starting with an initial pipeline count.

        Args:
            pipeline_count: Number of initial pipelines being submitted.
        """
        colored_count = self._colorize(str(pipeline_count), Colors.BRIGHT_WHITE)
        message = f"Starting with {colored_count} initial pipelines"
        self.info(message, "manager")

    def manager_exiting(self):
        """Log that the manager has finished and is exiting."""
        self.info("All pipelines finished. Exiting.", "manager")

    def activity_summary(self, active_pipelines, active_adaptive, buffered_pipelines):
        """Log a summary of the manager's current activity.

        Args:
            active_pipelines: Number of currently running pipeline tasks.
            active_adaptive: Number of currently running adaptive tasks.
            buffered_pipelines: Number of child pipelines buffered for
                submission.
        """
        colored_pipelines = self._colorize(str(active_pipelines), Colors.BRIGHT_GREEN)
        colored_adaptive = self._colorize(str(active_adaptive), Colors.BRIGHT_MAGENTA)
        colored_buffered = self._colorize(str(buffered_pipelines), Colors.BRIGHT_YELLOW)
        summary = (
            f"Active: {colored_pipelines} pipelines, "
            f"{colored_adaptive} adaptive tasks, "
            f"{colored_buffered} buffered"
        )
        self.debug(summary, "manager")

    def pipeline_log(self, message, level=LogLevel.INFO):
        """Log a message tagged with this logger's pipeline name.

        Used by `ImpressBasePipeline` subclasses to log from within a
        pipeline's own `run()` method, tagging output as
        `PIPELINE-<name>` rather than a manager component.

        Args:
            message: Message text to log.
            level: Severity level (default `LogLevel.INFO`).
        """
        if not self._is_enabled(level):
            return
        pipeline_component = f"PIPELINE-{self.name.upper()}"
        formatted = self._format_message(level, pipeline_component, message)
        self._write_log(formatted)

    def separator(self, title=None):
        """Write a horizontal separator line, optionally with a title.

        Args:
            title: Optional text to center within the separator.
        """
        if title:
            separator = f"{'=' * 20} {title} {'=' * 20}"
        else:
            separator = "=" * 50
        colored_sep = self._colorize(separator, Colors.BRIGHT_BLUE)
        self._write_log(colored_sep)

def __init__(
    self,
    name="ImpressManager",
    use_colors=True,
    output_stream=None,
    min_level: LogLevel = LogLevel.DEBUG,
):
    """
    Initialize the logger.

    Args:
        name: Logical name attached to `pipeline_log()` messages
            (typically the owning pipeline or manager name).
        use_colors: Whether to wrap output in ANSI color codes.
        output_stream: Stream to write all log messages to. Defaults
            to `sys.stdout`.
        min_level: Minimum severity to emit; messages below this
            level are silently dropped. Defaults to `LogLevel.DEBUG`
            (emit everything).
    """
    self.name = name
    self.use_colors = use_colors
    self.output_stream = output_stream or sys.stdout
    self.min_level = min_level

    self.level_colors = {
        LogLevel.DEBUG: Colors.BRIGHT_BLACK,
        LogLevel.INFO: Colors.BRIGHT_CYAN,
        LogLevel.WARNING: Colors.BRIGHT_YELLOW,
        LogLevel.ERROR: Colors.BRIGHT_RED,
        LogLevel.CRITICAL: Colors.RED + Colors.BOLD,
    }

    self.component_colors = {
        "pipeline": Colors.BRIGHT_GREEN,
        "adaptive": Colors.BRIGHT_MAGENTA,
        "manager": Colors.BRIGHT_BLUE,
        "workflow": Colors.CYAN,
        "task": Colors.YELLOW,
        "error": Colors.RED,
        "success": Colors.GREEN,
        "stage": Colors.BRIGHT_CYAN,
        "step": Colors.CYAN,
        "resource": Colors.MAGENTA,
        "data": Colors.BRIGHT_YELLOW,
        "validation": Colors.BRIGHT_MAGENTA,

class ImpressManager:
    """
    Manages the execution of multiple pipelines with adaptive optimization.

    Coordinates pipeline lifecycle, adaptive function execution, and child pipeline
    creation in an asynchronous environment.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        flow: WorkflowEngine,
        use_colors: bool = True,
        telemetry_config: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
        telemetry_subscribers: Optional[list[Callable]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Initialize the ImpressManager.

        The caller owns the engine: create it, pass it here, and shut it
        down when done. The manager never creates or shuts down the flow.

        Args:
            flow: WorkflowEngine the pipelines run on
            use_colors: Whether to use colors in logging output
            telemetry_config: kwargs forwarded to flow.start_telemetry() (e.g.
                checkpoint_path, resource_poll_interval). Pass None to disable.
            telemetry_subscribers: Callables registered via telemetry.subscribe()
                immediately after telemetry starts.

        A `PipelineSetup`'s `adaptive_fn` must be an engine task, declared by
        the caller the way asyncflow's own examples declare one:

            @flow.function_task(backend="local")
            async def adaptive_decision(pipeline):
                ...

        The manager awaits that task and does not choose where it runs:
        routing is declared, never discovered. The backend named must be a
        **thread** pool, because an adaptive function mutates the live
        pipeline object and a process pool would mutate a pickled copy. The
        loop is shared by every pipeline, so a callback left on it — even an
        `async def` that never awaits — stalls task dispatch for all of them;
        handing it to the engine is what prevents that.
        """
        self.flow: WorkflowEngine = flow
        self.pipeline_tasks: dict[ImpressBasePipeline, asyncio.Task] = {}
        self.adaptive_tasks: dict[ImpressBasePipeline, asyncio.Task] = {}
        self.new_pipeline_buffer: list[PipelineSetup] = []
        self.logger: ImpressLogger = ImpressLogger(use_colors=use_colors)
        self._telemetry_config: dict[str, Any] = telemetry_config or {}
        self._telemetry_subscribers: list[Callable] = telemetry_subscribers or []
        self.telemetry: Any = None

    def _normalize_pipeline_setup(
        self, setup: Union[dict[str, Any], PipelineSetup]
    ) -> PipelineSetup:
        """
        Normalize pipeline setup to PipelineSetup object.

        Args:
            setup: Either a dictionary or PipelineSetup object

        Returns:
            PipelineSetup object
        """
        if isinstance(setup, dict):
            return PipelineSetup.from_dict(setup)
        elif isinstance(setup, PipelineSetup):
            return setup
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected dict or PipelineSetup, got {type(setup)}")

    def submit_new_pipelines(
        self, pipeline_setups: list[Union[dict[str, Any], PipelineSetup]]
    ) -> None:
        """
        Submit new pipelines for execution.

        Args:
            pipeline_setups: List of pipeline configuration
                dictionaries or PipelineSetup objects

        Raises:
            ValueError: If pipeline type is not a subclass
                of ImpressBasePipeline
            TypeError: If a setup's `adaptive_fn` is not an engine task.
                `PipelineSetup` raises it; the whole batch is normalized
                below before any pipeline starts, so the first bad setup
                stops the batch.
        """
        setups = [self._normalize_pipeline_setup(s) for s in pipeline_setups]

        for setup in setups:
            # Create pipeline instance with config and kwargs merged
            pipeline_kwargs = {**setup.config, **setup.kwargs}
            pipeline: ImpressBasePipeline = setup.type(
                name=setup.name, flow=self.flow, **pipeline_kwargs
            )

            pipeline._adaptive_fn = setup.adaptive_fn
            pipeline._telemetry = self.telemetry

            self.logger.pipeline_started(pipeline.name)

            task: asyncio.Task = asyncio.create_task(pipeline.run())
            self.pipeline_tasks[pipeline] = task

    async def _run_adaptive_fn(self, pipeline: ImpressBasePipeline) -> None:
        """
        Run adaptive function for a pipeline in the background.

        The adaptive function updates the pipeline's
        submit_child_pipeline_request property.

        `adaptive_fn` is an engine task the caller declared, so the engine
        owns its execution and this method only awaits it. The call carries
        `workflow_id={pipeline}:adaptive` as a telemetry label: asyncflow
        names every task after its function (`workflow_manager.py:749`)
        regardless, and several pipelines usually share one callback, so
        without the label an adaptive call cannot be attributed to a
        pipeline in the trace. It is not collision avoidance — tasks are
        identified by a uid (`:750`), never by name — and the backend field
        is no substitute, since an adaptive task's lifecycle events name the
        default backend rather than the one it ran on (F13).

        Args:
            pipeline: Pipeline to run adaptive function for
        """
        try:
            self.logger.adaptive_started(pipeline.name)
            adaptive_fn: Optional[Callable[[ImpressBasePipeline], Any]] = getattr(
                pipeline, "_adaptive_fn", None
            )
            if adaptive_fn:
                await adaptive_fn(pipeline, workflow_id=f"{pipeline.name}:adaptive")
                self.logger.adaptive_completed(pipeline.name)
        except Exception as e:
            self.logger.adaptive_failed(pipeline.name, str(e))
        finally:
            pipeline.invoke_adaptive_step = False
            pipeline._adaptive_barrier.set()

    async def start(
        self, pipeline_setups: list[Union[dict[str, Any], PipelineSetup]]
    ) -> None:
        """
        Start the pipeline manager and execute all pipelines.

        Manages the complete lifecycle of pipelines including:
        - Initial pipeline submission
        - Adaptive function execution
        - Child pipeline creation
        - Pipeline completion and cleanup

        Args:
            pipeline_setups: List of initial pipeline
                configurations (dicts or PipelineSetup objects)
        """
        self.logger.separator("IMPRESS MANAGER STARTING")

        if self._telemetry_config:
            self.telemetry = await self.flow.start_telemetry(**self._telemetry_config)
            for fn in self._telemetry_subscribers:
                self.telemetry.subscribe(fn)

        self.logger.manager_starting(len(pipeline_setups))

        self.submit_new_pipelines(pipeline_setups)

        while True:
            any_activity: bool = False
            completed_pipelines: list[tuple] = []

            for pipeline, pipeline_future in list(self.pipeline_tasks.items()):
                # Check if pipeline needs adaptive step and isn't running one yet
                if (
                    getattr(pipeline, "invoke_adaptive_step", False)
                    and pipeline not in self.adaptive_tasks
                ):
                    adaptive_task: asyncio.Task = asyncio.create_task(
                        self._run_adaptive_fn(pipeline)
                    )
                    self.adaptive_tasks[pipeline] = adaptive_task
                    any_activity = True

                # Check if pipeline has new config ready
                config: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = pipeline.get_child_pipeline_request()

                if config:
                    self.logger.child_pipeline_submitted(config["name"], pipeline.name)
                    # Convert dict to PipelineSetup for consistency
                    child_setup = PipelineSetup.from_dict(config)
                    self.new_pipeline_buffer.append(child_setup)
                    any_activity = True

                # Check if parent should be killed
                if getattr(pipeline, "kill_parent", False):
                    self.logger.pipeline_killed(pipeline.name)
                    pipeline_future.cancel()
                    completed_pipelines.append((pipeline, pipeline_future))
                    continue

                # Check if pipeline is done - but only mark as completed
                # if adaptive task is also done
                if pipeline_future.done():
                    # Adaptive task still running — wait before marking completed
                    if pipeline in self.adaptive_tasks:
                        adaptive_task = self.adaptive_tasks[pipeline]
                        if not adaptive_task.done():
                            continue

                    completed_pipelines.append((pipeline, pipeline_future))

            # Clean up completed pipelines - but only if their
            # adaptive tasks are also done
            actually_completed: list[ImpressBasePipeline] = []
            for pipeline, future in completed_pipelines:
                # Double-check: only clean up if adaptive task is
                # done or doesn't exist
                if pipeline in self.adaptive_tasks:
                    adaptive_task = self.adaptive_tasks[pipeline]
                    if not adaptive_task.done():
                        continue
                    self.adaptive_tasks.pop(pipeline)

                self.pipeline_tasks.pop(pipeline, None)
                exc = None
                if future.done() and not future.cancelled():
                    try:
                        exc = future.exception()
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                if exc is not None:
                    self.logger.pipeline_failed(pipeline.name, exc)
                else:
                    self.logger.pipeline_completed(pipeline.name)
                actually_completed.append(pipeline)

            completed_pipelines = actually_completed

            # Clean up completed adaptive tasks
            completed_adaptive: list[ImpressBasePipeline] = []
            for pipeline, adaptive_task in list(self.adaptive_tasks.items()):
                if adaptive_task.done():
                    completed_adaptive.append(pipeline)

            for pipeline in completed_adaptive:
                self.adaptive_tasks.pop(pipeline, None)

            # Submit new pipelines; capture count before clearing so
            # activity_summary reports the real number submitted.
            if self.new_pipeline_buffer:
                buffered_count = len(self.new_pipeline_buffer)
                self.submit_new_pipelines(self.new_pipeline_buffer)
                self.new_pipeline_buffer.clear()
                any_activity = True
            else:
                buffered_count = 0

            # Log activity summary periodically
            if any_activity:
                self.logger.activity_summary(
                    len(self.pipeline_tasks),
                    len(self.adaptive_tasks),
                    buffered_count,
                )

            # Exit condition
            if (
                not self.pipeline_tasks
                and not self.new_pipeline_buffer
                and not self.adaptive_tasks
            ):
                self.logger.manager_exiting()
                self.logger.separator("IMPRESS MANAGER FINISHED")
                break

            if not any_activity:
                await asyncio.sleep(0.5)

A PipelineSetup's adaptive_fn must be an engine task, declared by the caller the way asyncflow's own examples declare one:

async def adaptive_decision(pipeline):
    ...

The manager awaits that task and does not choose where it runs: routing is declared, never discovered. The backend named must be a thread pool, because an adaptive function mutates the live pipeline object and a process pool would mutate a pickled copy. The loop is shared by every pipeline, so a callback left on it — even an async def that never awaits — stalls task dispatch for all of them; handing it to the engine is what prevents that.

def __init__(
    self,
    flow: WorkflowEngine,
    use_colors: bool = True,
    telemetry_config: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
    telemetry_subscribers: Optional[list[Callable]] = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Initialize the ImpressManager.

    The caller owns the engine: create it, pass it here, and shut it
    down when done. The manager never creates or shuts down the flow.

    Args:
        flow: WorkflowEngine the pipelines run on
        use_colors: Whether to use colors in logging output
        telemetry_config: kwargs forwarded to flow.start_telemetry() (e.g.
            checkpoint_path, resource_poll_interval). Pass None to disable.
        telemetry_subscribers: Callables registered via telemetry.subscribe()
            immediately after telemetry starts.

    A `PipelineSetup`'s `adaptive_fn` must be an engine task, declared by
    the caller the way asyncflow's own examples declare one:

        @flow.function_task(backend="local")
        async def adaptive_decision(pipeline):
            ...

    The manager awaits that task and does not choose where it runs:
    routing is declared, never discovered. The backend named must be a
    **thread** pool, because an adaptive function mutates the live
    pipeline object and a process pool would mutate a pickled copy. The
    loop is shared by every pipeline, so a callback left on it — even an
    `async def` that never awaits — stalls task dispatch for all of them;
    handing it to the engine is what prevents that.
    """
    self.flow: WorkflowEngine = flow
    self.pipeline_tasks: dict[ImpressBasePipeline, asyncio.Task] = {}
    self.adaptive_tasks: dict[ImpressBasePipeline, asyncio.Task] = {}
    self.new_pipeline_buffer: list[PipelineSetup] = []
    self.logger: ImpressLogger = ImpressLogger(use_colors=use_colors)
    self._telemetry_config: dict[str, Any] = telemetry_config or {}
    self._telemetry_subscribers: list[Callable] = telemetry_subscribers or []
    self.telemetry: Any = None

class ImpressBasePipeline(ABC):
    """
    Abstract base class for all IMPRESS pipelines.

    Subclasses implement `register_pipeline_tasks()` to bind task methods
    (via `auto_register_task()`) and `run()` to define the pipeline's
    control flow, and may optionally override `finalize()` for cleanup. The
    base class provides the adaptive
    execution protocol (`run_adaptive_step()`) and the child-pipeline
    request mechanism (`submit_child_pipeline_request()` /
    `get_child_pipeline_request()`) used by `ImpressManager` to support
    dynamic, self-spawning pipeline trees.

    Attributes:
        name: Pipeline instance name.
        flow: The `radical.asyncflow` `WorkflowEngine` used to submit
            executable tasks.
        state: Free-form dict for passing data between pipeline stages.
        config: Extra keyword arguments captured at construction time.
        kill_parent: When set to True, the manager cancels this pipeline's
            task on its next poll.
        invoke_adaptive_step: When True, the manager runs this pipeline's
            adaptive function on its next poll.
        incoming_child_pipeline_request: Pending child-pipeline submission
            request, populated by `submit_child_pipeline_request()`.
    """

    def __init__(self, name: str, flow=None, **config):
        """
        Initialize the pipeline and register its tasks.

        Args:
            name: Pipeline instance name.
            flow: The `radical.asyncflow` `WorkflowEngine` used to submit
                executable tasks.
            **config: Additional configuration stored in `self.config` and
                available to subclasses.
        """
        self.name = name
        self.flow = flow
        self.state = {}
        self.config = config
        self.kill_parent = False
        self.invoke_adaptive_step = False
        self.incoming_child_pipeline_request = {}
        self._adaptive_barrier = asyncio.Event()
        # Set by ImpressManager once telemetry has started; see `telemetry`.
        self._telemetry = None

        # Call the registration method - subclasses must implement this
        self.register_pipeline_tasks()

        self.logger = ImpressLogger(self.name)

    def submit_child_pipeline_request(self, pipeline_config):
        """
        Submit a request to spawn a child pipeline.

        Args:
            pipeline_config (dict): Configuration for the new pipeline including
                                  'name', 'type', 'config', and 'adaptive_fn'
        """
        self.incoming_child_pipeline_request = pipeline_config

    def get_child_pipeline_request(self):
        """
        Get and clear any pending spawn request for child pipelines.

        Returns:
            dict or None: The spawn request configuration if one exists, None otherwise.
                         After calling this method, the spawn request is cleared.
        """
        if self.incoming_child_pipeline_request:
            request = self.incoming_child_pipeline_request

            # reset the value to avoid submission request duplication
            self.incoming_child_pipeline_request = None
            return request

        return None

    @property
    def telemetry(self):
        """The running telemetry manager, or None when telemetry is off.

        `ImpressManager` sets it before `run()`. A pipeline driven without the
        manager has none unless the caller sets `_telemetry` itself.
        """
        return self._telemetry

    def auto_register_task(self, local_task=False, capture_stdio=True, **task_kwargs):
        """
        Decorator factory that binds a task function as a callable pipeline method.

        Used inside `register_pipeline_tasks()` to register the coroutines
        that make up a pipeline's stages.

        Args:
            local_task: If False (default), wraps the function via
                `self.flow.executable_task(**task_kwargs)`, turning it into
                an HPC-executable task submitted through the workflow
                engine. If True, the function runs as a plain local
                coroutine (e.g. for CPU-only analysis steps); each call is
                timed and emitted as an `impress.LocalStage` telemetry event.
            capture_stdio: For executable tasks, write the task's stdout and
                stderr to files in the backend's work dir (default True).
                The task's future then resolves to the stdout file path,
                not the stdout text. Pass False to get the text back.
            **task_kwargs: Forwarded to `self.flow.executable_task()` when
                `local_task` is False.

        Executable tasks get two more behaviours:

        - Each call is labelled `{pipeline}:{stage}` in telemetry unless the
          caller passes its own `workflow_id=`. Without a label, asyncflow
          names a task after its executable, which is usually `bash`.
        - When a task fails, the last lines of its captured stderr are
          logged, and attached to the exception as a note (Python 3.11+).

        Returns:
            A decorator that binds the wrapped function to `self` under its
            own name (so it becomes callable as `await self.<func_name>()`).
        """

        def decorator(func):
            if local_task:
                task = wrap_local_task(self, func)
            else:
                flow_task = self.flow.executable_task(
                    capture_stdio=capture_stdio, **task_kwargs
                )(func)
                task = self._wrap_executable_task(func, flow_task)
            setattr(self, func.__name__, task)
            return task

        return decorator

    def _wrap_executable_task(self, func, flow_task):
        """Label each call and report a failed task's stderr.

        Returns the engine's own future unchanged, so a stage future can
        still be passed to another task as a dependency.
        """
        stage = func.__name__

        @functools.wraps(flow_task)
        def call(*args, **kwargs):
            kwargs.setdefault("workflow_id", f"{self.name}:{stage}")
            fut = flow_task(*args, **kwargs)
            fut.add_done_callback(functools.partial(self._report_task_failure, stage))
            return fut

        return call

    def _report_task_failure(self, stage, fut):
        if fut.cancelled():
            return
        exc = fut.exception()
        if exc is None:
            return
        tail = stderr_tail(self.flow, fut, exc)
        message = f"{stage} failed: {exc!r}"
        if tail:
            message = f"{message}\n{tail}"
            if hasattr(exc, "add_note"):
                exc.add_note(tail)
        self.logger.pipeline_log(message, level=LogLevel.ERROR)

    def logged_command(self, log_file, cmd):
        """Wrap `cmd` so its combined output lands in `log_file`.

        For a per-task log next to the task's outputs. On failure the log's
        last lines also go to stderr, and so into the task's error.
        """
        return logged_command(log_file, cmd)

    async def run_adaptive_step(self, wait: bool = True):
        """Trigger adaptive step and optionally wait for completion.

        Args:
            wait: If True, waits for adaptive step completion.
                If False, triggers and returns immediately.
        """
        self._set_adaptive_flag(True)
        if wait:
            await self._await_adaptive_unlock()

    def _set_adaptive_flag(self, value: bool = True):
        """Set the adaptive flag and manage the barrier state"""
        self.invoke_adaptive_step = value
        if value:
            self._adaptive_barrier.clear()

    async def _await_adaptive_unlock(self) -> Any:
        """Pause until manager completes adaptive step and returns result."""
        await self._adaptive_barrier.wait()

    @abstractmethod
    async def run(self):
        """
        Main execution method; must be implemented by subclasses.

        Drives the pipeline's control flow: calling task methods registered
        in `register_pipeline_tasks()`, and calling
        `await self.run_adaptive_step(...)` at decision points where the
        pipeline should evaluate intermediate results and optionally spawn
        child pipelines.
        """
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def register_pipeline_tasks(self):
        """
        Register pipeline tasks; must be implemented by subclasses.

        Called once, synchronously, from `__init__` before anything else
        runs. Implementations use `@self.auto_register_task()` to bind task
        coroutines as callable methods on `self` for use in `run()`.
        """
        pass

    # Optional methods that subclasses can override
    async def get_scores_map(self):
        """

def __init__(self, name: str, flow=None, **config):
    """
    Initialize the pipeline and register its tasks.

    Args:
        name: Pipeline instance name.
        flow: The `radical.asyncflow` `WorkflowEngine` used to submit
            executable tasks.
        **config: Additional configuration stored in `self.config` and
            available to subclasses.
    """
    self.name = name
    self.flow = flow
    self.state = {}
    self.config = config
    self.kill_parent = False
    self.invoke_adaptive_step = False
    self.incoming_child_pipeline_request = {}
    self._adaptive_barrier = asyncio.Event()
    # Set by ImpressManager once telemetry has started; see `telemetry`.
    self._telemetry = None

    # Call the registration method - subclasses must implement this
    self.register_pipeline_tasks()

    self.logger = ImpressLogger(self.name)

def auto_register_task(self, local_task=False, capture_stdio=True, **task_kwargs):
    """
    Decorator factory that binds a task function as a callable pipeline method.

    Used inside `register_pipeline_tasks()` to register the coroutines
    that make up a pipeline's stages.

    Args:
        local_task: If False (default), wraps the function via
            `self.flow.executable_task(**task_kwargs)`, turning it into
            an HPC-executable task submitted through the workflow
            engine. If True, the function runs as a plain local
            coroutine (e.g. for CPU-only analysis steps); each call is
            timed and emitted as an `impress.LocalStage` telemetry event.
        capture_stdio: For executable tasks, write the task's stdout and
            stderr to files in the backend's work dir (default True).
            The task's future then resolves to the stdout file path,
            not the stdout text. Pass False to get the text back.
        **task_kwargs: Forwarded to `self.flow.executable_task()` when
            `local_task` is False.

    Executable tasks get two more behaviours:

    - Each call is labelled `{pipeline}:{stage}` in telemetry unless the
      caller passes its own `workflow_id=`. Without a label, asyncflow
      names a task after its executable, which is usually `bash`.
    - When a task fails, the last lines of its captured stderr are
      logged, and attached to the exception as a note (Python 3.11+).

    Returns:
        A decorator that binds the wrapped function to `self` under its
        own name (so it becomes callable as `await self.<func_name>()`).
    """

    def decorator(func):
        if local_task:
            task = wrap_local_task(self, func)
        else:
            flow_task = self.flow.executable_task(
                capture_stdio=capture_stdio, **task_kwargs
            )(func)
            task = self._wrap_executable_task(func, flow_task)
        setattr(self, func.__name__, task)
        return task

    return decorator

def get_child_pipeline_request(self):
    """
    Get and clear any pending spawn request for child pipelines.

    Returns:
        dict or None: The spawn request configuration if one exists, None otherwise.
                     After calling this method, the spawn request is cleared.
    """
    if self.incoming_child_pipeline_request:
        request = self.incoming_child_pipeline_request

        # reset the value to avoid submission request duplication
        self.incoming_child_pipeline_request = None
        return request

    return None

class PipelineSetup(BaseModel):
    """Pydantic model for pipeline configuration."""

    name: str = Field(..., description="Name of the pipeline")
    type: Annotated[
        type[ImpressBasePipeline], Field(..., description="Pipeline class type")
    ]
    config: dict[str, Any] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Pipeline configuration",
    )
    adaptive_fn: Optional[
        Callable[[ImpressBasePipeline], Union[Awaitable[None], None]]
    ] = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Optional adaptive function for the pipeline. Must be an engine "
            "task the caller declared with flow.function_task(...), on a "
            "thread-pool backend. ImpressManager awaits it and chooses "
            "nothing."
        ),
    )
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Additional keyword arguments",
    )

    model_config = {"arbitrary_types_allowed": True}

    @field_validator("type")
    @classmethod
    def validate_pipeline_type(cls, v: Any) -> type[ImpressBasePipeline]:
        """Validate that type is a subclass of ImpressBasePipeline."""
        if not isinstance(v, type) or not issubclass(v, ImpressBasePipeline):
            raise ValueError(f"Expected an ImpressBasePipeline subclass, got {type(v)}")
        return v

    @field_validator("adaptive_fn")
    @classmethod
    def validate_adaptive_fn(
        cls, v: Optional[Callable], info: ValidationInfo
    ) -> Optional[Callable]:
        """Reject an `adaptive_fn` that is not a declared engine task.

        The manager has no path of its own to run a callback on, so this
        fails at construction rather than letting the call fail inside the
        adaptive task, where the error is caught, logged, and the pipeline
        continues as though a decision had been made.

        Checking here rather than at submission also covers a child config,
        which reaches `from_dict()` before the manager sees it.
        """
        if v is None or _is_flow_task(v):
            return v

        # `name` is declared first, so it has been validated by now; it is
        # absent only if it failed its own validation.
        name = info.data.get("name", "<unnamed>")
        hint = (
            "Declare it on a thread-pool backend, e.g. "
            "flow.function_task(backend='local')(adaptive_decision), and "
            "pass the result as adaptive_fn."
        )

        if hasattr(v, "__task_description__"):
            # Marked, but still a coroutine function: this is the bare body,
            # not the task the decorator returned. Declaring it anywhere
            # marks it, so the mark alone does not catch this.
            raise TypeError(
                f"adaptive_fn for pipeline {name!r} is the undecorated "
                f"function, not the engine task declared from it. Pass the "
                f"object flow.function_task(...) returned — a child config "
                f"must carry the task, not the bare function."
            )

        kind = "coroutine function" if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(v) else "callable"
        raise TypeError(
            f"adaptive_fn for pipeline {name!r} is a plain {kind}, "
            f"not an engine task. {hint}"
        )

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Convert to dictionary format for backward compatibility."""
        result: dict[str, Any] = {
            "name": self.name,
            "type": self.type,
            "config": self.config,
        }
        if self.adaptive_fn is not None:
            result["adaptive_fn"] = self.adaptive_fn

        result.update(self.kwargs)
        return result

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "PipelineSetup":
        """Create PipelineSetup from dictionary (for backward compatibility)."""
        known_fields = {"name", "type", "config", "adaptive_fn"}
        pipeline_data = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k in known_fields}

        kwargs = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k not in known_fields}
        pipeline_data["kwargs"] = kwargs

        return cls(**pipeline_data)
